newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo launches new anaesthetic in UK.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo launches new anaesthetic in UK.

text.p: Britain's Glaxo Wellcome Plc launched a new anaesthetic in Britain on Tuesday which it could help patients wake up alert soon after surgery.
It said the new drug, Ultiva (remifentanil), could help cut down turn-around times in busy hospitals and emergency clinics.
It already has approval in the rest of the European Union and the United States.
Unlike other opioids -- drugs used to kill pain -- Ultiva becomes rapidly effective and then stops working almost as soon as it is stopped, Glaxo said in a statement.

"My patients are waking more quickly and less groggy, which means that most of my patients given remifentanil do not need to recover in intensive care," said Dr Gilbert Park, an anaesthetist at Addenbrooke's Hospital in Cambridge. -- London Newsroom 0171-542-8958
